title: Person–Situation Interaction Theatre
summary: Four fictional characters are put through five situations. Students rank their behaviour twice — once where traits show through and once where a different affordance reorders everyone — then take control of situation strength and assigned role to find the setting where the four become behaviourally indistinguishable.
learningObjectives: Explain what makes a situation strong or weak, and what a strong situation does to observed between-person variation.
Distinguish situational constraint from situational affordance, and explain why two equally weak situations can rank the same people differently.
Explain why low observed behavioural variance is not evidence of low trait variance.
Say why neither 'personality matters more' nor 'situations matter more' is a defensible summary of the evidence.
Relate behavioural consistency to aggregation across situations and occasions.
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; every calculation runs in the browser tab, and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Ranking uses one native select per character rather than drag-and-drop, so there is no dragging to provide an alternative to; duplicate ranks produce an accessible error message rather than a silent failure. Charts and the interaction diagram are hidden from assistive technology and paired with visible tables carrying the same numbers; edge weights are printed as text beside each edge, and negative weights are dashed as well as signed. Keyboard operable throughout; changes announced through the shell's polite live region; reduced motion honoured; forced-colours rules provided; usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Person-situation interaction: situational strength, affordances, and why the debate was badly posed
simulationNotes: Four fictional characters with illustrative trait scores on an arbitrary 0-100 scale; no norms and no reference sample. Behaviour is modelled as k·norm + (1−k)·disposition + role, where k is situation strength and disposition is a weighted sum of only those traits the situation affords. The anonymous-discussion situation carries a negative weight on politeness, which is what reorders the cast. No occasion-to-occasion variability, no measurement error and no trait interactions are modelled. Situation strength is stipulated by the author rather than estimated.
